brief: 5 things the skincare industry doesn't want you to know.

slots.headline: WHAT THE INDUSTRY HIDES?
slots.subtitle: Five truths that keep you buying bottles you don't need.

slots.title: NATURAL MEANS NOTHING
slots.body: The word 'natural' has zero legal definition in skincare. A brand can slap it on a bottle loaded with synthetic fragrance and irritants. Don't trust the label; trust the ingredient list.

slots.title: PRICE ISN'T RESULTS
slots.body: A two-hundred-dollar cream and a twenty-dollar serum can share the exact same active ingredient. You're often paying for glass bottles and celebrity campaigns, not science.

slots.title: YOU CAN'T SHRINK PORES
slots.body: Pore size is determined by genetics and age. Products claiming to shrink them only temporarily clear them out. It's biology, not a bottle, that sets the size.

slots.title: BURNING ISN'T PURGING
slots.body: Brands love to call redness and peeling purging. In reality, your skin barrier is crying for help. Real improvement doesn't require constant stinging and sensitivity.

slots.title: MAKEUP SPF WON'T SAVE YOU
slots.body: You'd need seven times the normal amount of foundation to reach the labeled SPF. No one applies that much. Always use a separate sunscreen before anything else.

slots.title: YOUR BARRIER COMES FIRST
slots.body: The industry pushes endless acids and retinols to keep you buying. But without a healthy barrier, actives do more harm than good. Less is usually more.

slots.headline: BETTER SKIN FEWER PRODUCTS
slots.body: Ditch the hype. Build a routine that actually works with our free barrier-first guide.
